questions.prompt: What is a Pod in Kubernetes?

options.text: A physical server in the cluster
The smallest deployable unit — one or more containers sharing a network identity and storage

questions.explanation: A Pod is the smallest deployable unit; it wraps one or more containers that share an IP and storage, and is usually a single container in practice.

options.text: A stable network address for Pods
Management of a set of identical Pods, including scaling, self-healing, and rolling updates

questions.explanation: A Deployment declares the desired Pods (image and replica count) and manages a ReplicaSet to scale, self-heal, and roll out updates.

questions.prompt: Why do you need a Service when you already have Pods?

options.text: Pods cannot run containers without one
Pods are ephemeral and change IPs; a Service gives a stable address and load-balances across the current Pods

questions.explanation: Because Pods come and go with changing IPs, a Service provides a fixed name/IP and spreads traffic across the matching Pods.

questions.prompt: The command-line tool used to talk to a Kubernetes cluster is ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: kubectl is the CLI for the API server; the declarative workflow is kubectl apply -f manifest.yaml.

questions.prompt: How does the Docker image you built relate to Kubernetes?

options.text: Kubernetes rebuilds your app from source
Kubernetes runs the exact OCI image you pushed; a Deployment's image field points at your registry
You must convert the image to a special Kubernetes format

questions.explanation: Kubernetes schedules and runs the same OCI image you built and pushed; the kubelet pulls it and runs it in a container inside a Pod.

questions.prompt: Match each Kubernetes concept to its role.

pairs.right: Manages the cluster and desired state
A worker machine that runs Pods
Keeps a set of identical Pods running
Stable address and load balancing for Pods

questions.explanation: The control plane decides, nodes run workloads, Deployments maintain Pods, and Services expose them with a stable endpoint.
